chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all from al-Fatah ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah, so he said: 'It is permissible, freely authorized for the one whom Allah has not made needless through marriage, so let him maintain chastity with Mut'ah. So if he is needless from it through marriage, then it is authorized for him when he is absent from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Mut'ah for those who can afford permanent marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of Mut'ah as a means to preserve chastity for those unable to afford permanent marriage, while also noting its continued validity for those who are married but separated. It highlights the practical flexibility of the institution in Shia jurisprudence, positioning it not merely as a temporary fix but as a legitimate marital contract with specific conditions. The ruling underscores the principle that if one is self-sufficient through permanent marriage, abstaining is preferred, yet the option remains open.
